description: Ready / clear_winner run with a wide margin, a single fragile connection, and a populated flip threshold. The confident-tone baseline: the served tone table forbids no phrasing at this row, so this fixture is where the LEXICON and NUMBER dimensions carry the load.

provenance.note: Revived and refreshed to the current input shape: graph edges now carry ids (the March graphs had none, so the runtime entity-grounding corpus was node-only), flip_threshold_data added (post-v11, invoke.ts:123), and the March fixture's hand-written margin of 0.15 dropped — it disagreed with its own winner/runner_up (0.72 - 0.28 = 0.44). Margin is now computed the way invoke.ts computes it. | FLIP_THRESHOLDS GOLDEN CORRECTED 2026-07-31 (fix-decision-review-v15 lane, disclosed): the golden flip_thresholds entries were hand-written as { factor_label, current, flip_at, note } with rounded values. Two independent defects. (a) FIELD NAMES: the runtime contract is { factor_id, factor_label, current_display, flip_display, narrative } (src/orchestrator-v5/compose/phase3-blocks.ts:1703-1765 reads factor_id/factor_label/narrative and DROPS any entry missing one), so the old goldens described a shape production would discard entirely — a golden nothing could ever produce. (b) VALUE FORM: the served v14 prompt contradicts itself here — :344-350 orders the raw value verbatim while :116-118/:220 order the percentage form and no_raw_probability_decimals scores the raw form as a failure. The goldens now follow the NON-self-contradictory rule (percentage form) and the runtime field names. The prompt-side resolution is drafted but NOT YET PROMOTED (tools/orchestrator-eval/drafts/decision_review.v15-draft.txt); until it is, this fixture encodes the contract the runtime and the scorer agree on, not the flip bullet the served prompt still carries.

input.brief: Should we expand into the European market? We have four hundred pro customers and want to reach eight hundred.

candidates.label: good
candidates.note: Grounded, plain-language, coherent. Should PASS every dimension.

output.narrative_summary: Enter European Market comes out ahead by about 44 percentage points over Delay to Next Year. Competitive intensity is the main fragility, though the ordering holds in about 91% of runs.

story_headlines.opt_expand: Comes out ahead on growth and holds across the simulated range
story_headlines.opt_wait: Protects near term spend but gives up the growth window

robustness_explanation.summary: The ordering is stable across the simulated range, holding in about 91% of runs.
robustness_explanation.primary_risk: Competitive intensity could compress revenue growth if rivals respond quickly.
stability_factors: Europe market entry moves the outcome most and is well supported.
fragility_factors: Competitive intensity carries the widest spread of the connections examined.

output.readiness_rationale: The comparison is stable, so the main open question is how quickly competitive intensity shifts.

fac_competition.why: Competitive intensity is the least well supported input shaping revenue growth.
fac_competition.expected_gain: Narrows the spread on the main fragility.

edge_competition_revenue.context: If competitive intensity rises sharply, the growth path narrows and the two options converge.

flip_thresholds.narrative: If Competitive Intensity moves from 35% to 62%, the leading option changes.

bias_findings.description: The stated customer target may be anchoring how the options are compared.

key_assumptions: Europe market entry continues to move the outcome as strongly as modelled.
Competitive response stays within the range examined.

decision_quality_prompts.prompt: What would have to be true about competitive intensity for the ordering to change?

pre_mortem.scenario: Twelve months on, competitive intensity rose faster than modelled and revenue growth stalled.
pre_mortem.leading_indicator: Rivals matching the entry offer within the first quarter.
